title: Stored x-only leaf birthday search on secp256k1 at 125.151838075279: six leaves per batched inverse, a two-fraction class label with a lattice mass bound, metered rare-carry branches and a paired range scan

claims.statement: For uniform production secp256k1 Q=[x]P, the classical cold stored-leaf birthday search of proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.390000001 over the challenge and fresh algorithm coins, with no heuristic: the Chen-Stein method on cross-node leaf pairs bounds P(no collision), and drops, caps, wrong class indices and the enumerated carry sites of the kernels (section 3.4) are charged failure rows, as are the caps of two meters, while RNDR, the ideal coin source, adds none (section 6). On every run its total work is at most 2^125.151838075279 target-group-operation equivalents (1000 AArch64 instructions per unit). Each pair of generator points X, Y gives six leaves, the x-coordinates of phi^t(X) + Y and phi^t(X) - Y for t = 0, 1, 2, from one batched inverse of y_Y^2 - y_X^2 (section 3.1). A class's label is the pair of the top 100 bits of the fractions v*/p and (beta v* mod p)/p, v* = min(x, beta x, beta^2 x) the canonical x-coordinate: every leaf has its own x's three fractions, x's top bits, KEY's top column of x*beta/p with one more column summed as words shifted right by 3 (within 68 below at 128 bits), and the third from the first two (within [-1, 70]), and KEY's index j picks the pair (j, j + 1): 44 instructions for j = 0 and 49 for j = 1, 2 (section 3.3). A leaf whose computed fraction lies near a 2^28 block boundary, or whose x lies just below a multiple of 2^156, may carry another label, a charged missed-collision row below 2^-19.8 per leaf; no leaf is dropped. KEY's index needs no windows: a wrong index, on a set of rate below 2^-54.29, is a charged missed collision. As the pairs (v, beta v mod p) lie on a lattice with the basis (B, A - B), (A - B, -A) from secp256k1's Frobenius pi = A + B*omega, a box of label values holds at most 1 + 2^-19 times its share, so the mass bound is KB(f) = 6*2^(256-f)(1 + 2^-19)/(r-1) and classes sharing the 184 matched bits give false candidates charged to the caps. Machine (section 2.1): 2^72 nodes, each with one processor (base AArch64 with FEAT_RNG and FEAT_LSE) and a memory below 2^64 bytes, whose links deliver a message's four words at the address its sender stored and keep no flags, rings or counters. Beyond its sender's instructions, every message's charge includes 8 instruction-equivalents at each hop: its delivery as route.s dlv (6), which the experiment executes for every message of its 4 x 4 run, and its port's in-flight count (2). Hop 1, hop 2 and grouping are charged 18, 18.25 and 17.546875 per record; the grouping's scan_ranges compares K2 only, within each d4 range, in CMP/CCMP pairs at 195/64 per record plus at most 26 per range and 8 per candidate, and its matches of different classes on the 184 label bits are charged to the candidate, request and relay caps (2^28, 2^29, 2^34; section 6.4). The rare carries and borrows of the field macros (SHX, FDX, F5, FS, FADDW) are taken by a branch over a fixup that completes the chain, so every result is bit-identical to an inline chain; a fixup costs 3 or 4 instructions and is counted, and a node starts a batch only while its fixups are at most 2^45 - 46 q2, so the ledger charges 4*2^45 per node and Markov's inequality on the fixups' mean (below 2^28.35 per node, from the operand sets of section 3.4) charges the cap (section 3.4). certificate.py gives at most 342.1075 instructions per leaf and the claim 125.151838075279. Peak memory at most 2^135.9988 bytes; preprocessing at most 2^110.2061 units, included; no advice; certificate.py checks that the work, memory and preprocessing figures are the least 12-decimal (work) or 4-decimal (memory, preprocessing) values at or above their exact values, and that 0.390000001 is below the success bound. The bound is for the machine of section 2.1. Lineage: our a3ca3235 (the base package: the fraction key on our 5b6cd013's metered rare-carry branches, windowless KEY and range-local scan of our 502d7155 and eb0aea59, with b00400fa's paired scanner), f9d5a673 (transport and grouping) and b3716a20 (the six-leaf fwd and bwd kernels, the site table and the success argument), package 8f733826 (field rows and FS) with c8a6819e (kernel macros, a64.py), 02feb284 (fe_inv, the F0 and F1 rows), 4595bad7 (SB6's stored-offset subtraction) and fce6e7ef (link-side counter updates charged), submissions 3828873f, 6ef3e7b3, d637fb0a, 9798f5f4 and d9e3dbf4 (STADD, paired scan comparisons, prefix4, the generator and candidate allowances, a claim on a decimal grid), 472226d8, 4fdb8a9c and e1ecd7cc (a success target nearer 0.39, a 12-decimal claim), 80e9e8af and 1efcef88 (the range-local scan), 892a3df8 and b00400fa (its paired 64-record form, taken unchanged), 1fbd26e8 (the candidate charge at twice its itemized work), and 807e4bf5 and a9297fb0 (rare exits to charged stubs and a per-walk meter); new here is the two-fraction label (the shifted-sum column, the one-word complemented third fraction with its bound, the label-error row and the lattice count behind its mass bound); no prior acceptance or score is a premise. This is an analytic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run the six-leaf kernels on production points, with every emitted label of a leaf outside KEY's window set and D against its class's label and the class-label test on random and boundary classes, and the emit, both hops (each message delivered by executing dlv) and the grouping (with the paired scan_ranges) on a 4 x 4 machine, against exact references; check the arithmetic sites and rare-carry fixups of section 3.4 (sites.py; planted points force fixups in both passes, planted leaves sit at the label-error boundaries); compare the counts of the leaf, inversion, transport, delivery and grouping kernels with certificate.py; run the q25 toy (toy.py) with six leaves per incidence and certificate.py. Budget-limited parts run stated minimums. Not a production-scale attack.
